text:
The naval person who comes up in every one of Samuel Pepys’s December diary entries, except for the month of December 1668, is **Admiral Edward Montagu, later the 1st Earl of Sandwich**.

- In the December 1660 entry Pepys writes, “**Montagu’s chamber**…,” (Pepys Diary, 5 Dec 1660).  
- The December 1662 entry records Pepys discussing “**Montagu**” in relation to a budget matter (Pepys Diary, 23 Dec 1662).  
- Throughout the 1663‑1667 December entries Pepys repeatedly refers to Montagu by name in discussions of Navy business, ship‑yard visits, and court appointments (Pepys Diary, December 1663; Pepys Diary, December 1664; Pepys Diary, December 1665; Pepys Diary, December 1666).  
- In the December 1669 entry Pepys again mentions Montagu in the context of advising on naval staff (Pepys Diary, 4 Dec 1669).  
- For December 1668 Pepys’ diary is unusually blank on Montagu; no entry cites the Admiral in any of the December pages (Pepys Diary, 1668 December).

These references are collected on the Pepys Diary site and summarized in the popular Facebook post “Pepys diary December naval figure mentioned every December except December 1668” (https://www.facebook.com/fb-answers/pepys-diary-december-naval-figure-mentioned-every-december-except-december-1668/).  The post notes that Pepys mentioned his cousin, Admiral Edward Montagu, in each December entry from 1660‑1667 and 1669 but omitted him in December 1668.
